% Isolated candidate statement for source-aware production verification.
% This file is not a live-book input and makes no novelty or priority claim.

Let \(B\) be a nonempty set.  Write \(X_B\) for the set obtained from
\(B\times[-\infty,0]\) by identifying all the points \((b,0)\) to one
point \(\eta\), and write
\[
                    p_b(t)=[(b,t)]\in X_B .
\]
We give \(X_B\) the topology of Chambert--Loir--Ducros,
Section~6.7.3: a subset \(V\subseteq X_B\) is open if and only if every
\[
 V_b=\{t\in[-\infty,0]:p_b(t)\in V\}
\]
is open in the order topology and, when \(\eta\in V\), the set of
\(b\in B\) for which \(V_b\ne[-\infty,0]\) is finite.  Thus this is not
the quotient topology when \(B\) is infinite.

A standard open neighbourhood of \(\eta\) is specified by a finite set
\(A\subseteq B\) and numbers \(R_a>0\), \(a\in A\), and has branches
\begin{equation}
 U_b=[-\infty,0]\quad(b\notin A),
 \qquad
 U_a=(-R_a,0]\quad(a\in A).
 \label{eq:p071-star-standard-neighbourhood}
\end{equation}
Every neighbourhood of \(\eta\) contains a standard one.

We use the exact smooth structure of that example.  A real-valued
function \(f\) on a neighbourhood of \(\eta\) is smooth precisely when
each \(f_b=f\circ p_b\) is ordinarily smooth on the finite stratum,
is constant on a neighbourhood of \(-\infty\) whenever that endpoint is
in its domain, only finitely many branches fail to be both full and
constant, and
\begin{equation}
                         \sum_{b\in B} f_b'(0)=0 .
 \label{eq:p071-star-smooth-balance}
\end{equation}
The sum in \eqref{eq:p071-star-smooth-balance} is finite.  For such a
smooth function, positivity of
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''f\) is equivalent to \(f_b''\geq0\) on every
finite branch stratum.  Let
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,0}\) be this sheaf of smooth psh functions,
let \(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}\) be the smallest subsheaf of the sheaf
of \(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\)-valued functions which contains
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,0}\) and is stable under pointwise decreasing
sequential limits, and let \(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}\) be the sheaf
of functions which are locally pointwise decreasing limits of sections
of \(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,0}\).

On a standard neighbourhood \(U\) as in
\eqref{eq:p071-star-standard-neighbourhood}, define
\(\mathscr J_B(U)\) as follows.  A function
\(u:U\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) belongs to \(\mathscr J_B(U)\) if:
\begin{enumerate}
\item every branch function \(u_b=u\circ p_b\) is extended-real convex
  on finite subintervals of its domain, and, for each full branch,
  \begin{equation}
   u_b(-\infty)=\lim_{t\to-\infty}u_b(t)
             \quad\text{in }\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\};
   \label{eq:p071-star-endpoint-trace}
  \end{equation}
\item if \(c=u(\eta)\in\mathbf R\), then for every finite
  \(F\subseteq B\setminus A\), every \(r_b>0\), \(b\in F\), and every
  \(0<\rho_a<R_a\), \(a\in A\), one has
  \begin{equation}
   \sum_{b\in F}\frac{c-u_b(-r_b)}{r_b}
       \leq
   \sum_{a\in A}\frac{u_a(-\rho_a)-c}{\rho_a}.
   \label{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance}
  \end{equation}
  The empty set \(F\) is allowed.
\end{enumerate}
On an arbitrary open subset of \(X_B\), define \(\mathscr J_B\) by these
conditions locally, using ordinary finite intervals away from \(\eta\),
the trace condition at an included endpoint \(-\infty\), and standard
neighbourhoods at \(\eta\).

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate}
For the preceding CLD tropical star, one has an equality of sheaves
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}
   =\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}
   =\mathscr J_B.
 \label{eq:p071-star-first-stage-collapse}
\end{equation}
More precisely, let \(u\in\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}(V)\) and let
\(x\in V\).

If \(x=\eta\) and \(u(\eta)=-\infty\), there is one fixed open
neighbourhood \(W\subseteq V\) of \(\eta\) on which \(u\equiv-\infty\).

If \(x=\eta\) and \(c=u(\eta)\in\mathbf R\), there is one fixed standard
neighbourhood \(W\subseteq V\), with exceptional set \(A\), such that
all finite-stratum values of \(u|_W\) are real.  The endpoint derivatives
\begin{equation}
 d_i=D_-u_i(0)
     :=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{c-u_i(-r)}{r}
 \label{eq:p071-star-endpoint-derivatives}
\end{equation}
are real, \(d_b\geq0\) for \(b\notin A\), and
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{b\in B\setminus A}d_b+\sum_{a\in A}d_a\leq0.
 \label{eq:p071-star-slope-balance}
\end{equation}
The first sum is the supremum of its finite subsums.  In particular it
is finite, and \(u_b\not\equiv c\) on at most countably many full
branches.  There are smooth psh functions \(g_n\) on that one fixed
neighbourhood \(W\) such that
\begin{equation}
                  g_{n+1}\leq g_n,
                  \qquad
                  g_n\longrightarrow u|_W
                  \quad\text{pointwise}.
 \label{eq:p071-star-fixed-neighbourhood-approximation}
\end{equation}
At a point different from \(\eta\), the same fixed-neighbourhood
conclusion holds on an ordinary interval or on a constant-collar
neighbourhood of \(-\infty\).
\end{theorem}

Work with the standing parlinear parameters
\(K=\mathbf Q\) and \(G=\mathbf R\) used in the body of
Chambert--Loir--Ducros.  Let \(Z\) be a locally compact Hausdorff space
with a basis of clopen subsets.  Give
\(Z\) the following affine \(G\)-tropical structure: its domains are the
locally closed subsets, and its parlinear and affine functions are the
locally constant real-valued functions.  Let
\(\Omega\subseteq\mathbf R^d\), \(d\geq0\), be a nonempty open convex set
with its
standard affine structure, and give
\[
                         X=Z\times\Omega
\]
the product affine \(G\)-tropical structure of
\cite[\S\S9.1.1--9.1.4]{CLD25}.  Thus a function on \(X\) is smooth precisely when,
locally on \(Z\times\Omega\), it is independent of the \(Z\)-variable and
smooth in the Euclidean variable.  Such a smooth function is psh precisely
when its Euclidean Hessian is positive semidefinite.

Write \(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}\),
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\), and \(\operatorname{Psh}_X\) for the smooth
psh generator sheaf, its first local decreasing-limit stage, and the full
generated CLD psh sheaf, respectively.  Then
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-collapse}
                    \operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}
                    =\operatorname{Psh}_X.
\end{equation}
More precisely, for every \(u\in\operatorname{Psh}_X(U)\) and every
\((z_0,x_0)\in U\), there are a compact clopen neighbourhood \(C\) of
\(z_0\) and an open Euclidean ball \(B_0\) about \(x_0\), with
\(C\times\overline{B_0}\subseteq U\), such that the following fixed-
neighbourhood re-selection holds.  For every ball \(B\) about \(x_0\) with
\(\overline B\subseteq B_0\), there are smooth psh functions
\(g_k\in\operatorname{Psh}_{X,0}(C\times B)\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-fixed-neighbourhood}
                          g_{k+1}\leq g_k,
             \qquad      g_k\downarrow u|_{C\times B}.
\end{equation}

The local comparison class used in the proof has an intrinsic
factorization description.  After shrinking \(C\times B\), every section
of \(\operatorname{Psh}_X\) can be written
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-factorization}
             u(z,x)=\bar u(q(z),x),
\end{equation}
where \(q:C\twoheadrightarrow Y\) is a continuous surjection onto a compact
metrizable zero-dimensional space, \(\bar u\) is upper semicontinuous on
\(Y\times B\), and, for every \(y\in Y\), the function
\(x\mapsto\bar u(y,x)\) is either finite-valued convex or identically
\(-\infty\).  Conversely, every function locally admitting
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-factorization} with these properties belongs to
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\).

In particular, the conclusion applies for arbitrary \(d\) and to the
nonmetrizable, nonambient examples
\[
                    Z=\{0,1\}^{\Lambda}
\]
for every index set \(\Lambda\), including uncountable \(\Lambda\), with
the locally constant affine structure just specified.  The result concerns
this exact product structure; it makes no assertion for a different affine
structure on the same underlying space, for general polyhedral face
gluings, or for arbitrary affine \(G\)-tropical spaces.

% Book-local P07.1 theorem, 13 September 2026.
% This theorem combines the exact infinite CLD star of Section 6.7.3 with
% one active open Euclidean factor.  It makes no novelty or priority claim.

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:p071-infinite-star-euclidean-collapse}
Let $B\ne\varnothing$ be an arbitrary set, let $X_B$ be the exact
Chambert--Loir--Ducros star of
\Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate}, and let
$\Omega\subset\mathbf R^d$ be a nonempty open convex set.  Put
\[
                             X=X_B\times\Omega .
\]
We use the following exact product generator sheaf.  On a product of an
ordinary interval in a branch with an open convex subset of $\Omega$, a
real-valued generator is a smooth jointly convex function.  At a full
endpoint $-\infty$, it is additionally constant in the branch variable
on a terminal collar, locally uniformly in the Euclidean variable.

At a node point, take a standard star neighbourhood $U$, with finite
exceptional set $A\subset B$ and exceptional collars
$(-R_a,0]$, and an open convex $V\subset\Omega$.  Write
\[
 g_b(t,y)=g(p_b(t),y),\qquad c_g(y)=g(\eta,y).
\]
A generator on $U\times V$ is required to have jointly smooth convex
branch functions, one finite set $K\subset B\setminus A$ such that
\begin{equation}
 g_b(t,y)=c_g(y)
 \quad
 \bigl(b\in B\setminus(A\cup K),\ t\in[-\infty,0],\ y\in V\bigr),
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-smooth-finite-activity}
\end{equation}
and the exact balance law
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{a\in A}\partial_tg_a(0,y)
   +\sum_{b\in K}\partial_tg_b(0,y)=0
 \qquad(y\in V).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-smooth-balance}
\end{equation}
On every full active branch, the terminal-collar condition above is also
imposed.  Let $\mathcal G_{X,0}$ be the sheaf defined by these local
conditions, let $\mathcal P_{X,1}$ be its sheaf of local pointwise
decreasing sequential limits, and let $\mathcal P_X$ be the smallest
subsheaf of $\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}$-valued functions which contains
$\mathcal G_{X,0}$ and is closed under such limits.

Define a comparison sheaf $\mathcal J_X$ by the following local
conditions.  Every branch function $u_b(t,y)$, with the node value
inserted at $t=0$, is extended-real jointly convex.  On a full branch,
\begin{equation}
 u_b(-\infty,y)=\lim_{t\to-\infty}u_b(t,y)
 \quad\text{in }\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-endpoint-trace}
\end{equation}
Near a node, require one standard product $U\times V$ and one countable
set $K\subset B\setminus A$ such that
\begin{equation}
 u_b(t,y)=c(y):=u(\eta,y)
 \quad
 \bigl(b\in B\setminus(A\cup K),\ t\in[-\infty,0],\ y\in V\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-countable-activity}
\end{equation}
Finally, let $F\subset B\setminus A$ be finite, choose $r_b>0$ for
$b\in F$, choose $0<\rho_a<R_a$ for $a\in A$, and put
\[
 \Lambda=\sum_{b\in F}\frac1{r_b}
              +\sum_{a\in A}\frac1{\rho_a}.
\]
If $\Lambda>0$, $c(y_0)\in\mathbf R$, and points
$y_0,y_b,y_a\in V$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda y_0=
   \sum_{b\in F}\frac{y_b}{r_b}
      +\sum_{a\in A}\frac{y_a}{\rho_a},
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-barycentre}
\end{equation}
then require the product junction inequality
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda c(y_0)\leq
   \sum_{b\in F}\frac{u_b(-r_b,y_b)}{r_b}
      +\sum_{a\in A}\frac{u_a(-\rho_a,y_a)}{\rho_a}.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-jensen}
\end{equation}
The case $F=A=\varnothing$ is vacuous.  Membership in
$\mathcal J_X$ means that every point has a neighbourhood of the
displayed type on which these conditions hold.

Then
\begin{equation}
                 \mathcal P_{X,1}=\mathcal P_X=\mathcal J_X.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-collapse}
\end{equation}
More precisely, every germ in these sheaves has a pointwise decreasing
approximation by members of $\mathcal G_{X,0}$ on one fixed smaller
product neighbourhood.  At a node point this neighbourhood may be chosen
as $U'\times V'$, with $U'$ standard and $V'$ open convex; at a
full endpoint it may be chosen as one fixed terminal product
neighbourhood.

For $d=0$, \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-jensen} is exactly the
finite-point balance of
\Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate}.  The theorem permits an
arbitrary branch set and mixed branch--Euclidean Hessian terms.  It does
not cover a polyhedral factor with faces or corners, a separately convex
generator sheaf, a non-CLD infinite star, an additional Stone parameter,
or nonambient branch structures.  Consequently it narrows but does not
retire P07.1.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
We divide the proof into the comparison statement, the numerical
consequences at the centre, and the approximation construction.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Convex functions on a full branch.}
Let \(v:[-\infty,0]\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be extended-real
convex on the finite stratum and satisfy the exact trace condition at
\(-\infty\).  On the open ordinary interval \((-\infty,0)\), local
extended-real convexity gives the following alternative: \(v\) is
finite everywhere or \(v\equiv-\infty\).  Indeed, suppose that
\(v(x)=-\infty\) and \(v(y)\) is finite.  Choose \(z\) on the side of
\(y\) opposite to \(x\), so that \(y\) lies strictly between \(x\) and
\(z\).  The convexity inequality has right side \(-\infty\), regardless
of the value at \(z\), and contradicts the finiteness of \(v(y)\).
In the first case convexity also forces \(v(0)\) to be finite: if
\(v(0)=-\infty\), apply the same argument to a finite point and an
intermediate finite point.  In the second case \(v(0)\) may be finite
or \(-\infty\); the former possibility is the polar endpoint jump.

In every case \(v\) is nondecreasing in the extended order.  This is
automatic in the polar case.  In the finite-interior case, otherwise
there would be \(s<t\leq0\) for which
\[
                       q=\frac{v(t)-v(s)}{t-s}<0.
\]
For \(x<s\), monotonicity of the secant slopes of a convex function gives
\[
             \frac{v(s)-v(x)}{s-x}\leq q,
             \qquad
             v(x)\geq v(s)-q(s-x)\longrightarrow+\infty,
\]
contrary to the trace in
\eqref{eq:p071-star-endpoint-trace}, whose value is not \(+\infty\).
Consequently, if \(v(0)=c\in\mathbf R\), then \(v(t)\leq c\) for
every \(t<0\).  The quantities
\begin{equation}
                  p_v(r)=\frac{c-v(-r)}r
\label{eq:p071-star-secant-slope}
\end{equation}
are nonnegative and increase as \(r\downarrow0\).  Their limit is the
left derivative \(D_-v(0)\in[0,+\infty]\); in the polar case all of
them and the derivative are \(+\infty\).

The same elementary secant-slope argument, without the nonnegativity
conclusion, applies on an exceptional collar.  For every finite convex
function \(v\) on \([-R,0]\),
\begin{equation}
 \frac{v(0)-v(-r)}r\leq D_-v(0)
 \qquad(0<r\leq R).
 \label{eq:p071-star-secant-below-derivative}
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent
\emph{The comparison conditions form a sheaf.}
We first verify restriction at the centre.  Suppose that \(u\) satisfies
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} on a standard neighbourhood
with exceptional set \(A\), and restrict to a smaller standard
neighbourhood whose exceptional set is \(A\cup E\), where \(E\) is
finite.  Apply \eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} before the
restriction to the union of a prescribed finite
\(F\subseteq B\setminus(A\cup E)\) and \(E\), choosing the desired
collar points on the branches in \(E\).  The same inequality with empty
full-branch set first shows that all sampled exceptional values are
finite, and its singleton instances show the same for the sampled
branches in \(E\).  Hence the following rearrangement is legitimate in
\(\mathbf R\).  Since
\[
 \frac{u_e(-\rho_e)-c}{\rho_e}
      =-\frac{c-u_e(-\rho_e)}{\rho_e},
\]
moving the terms indexed by \(E\) to the right gives precisely
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} for the restricted
neighbourhood.  Further shrinking of collars causes no difficulty.

For gluing, only the converse local-to-global implication at \(\eta\)
needs proof.  Let \(U\) be standard with exceptional set \(A\), and
suppose the comparison conditions hold on a smaller standard
\(W\subseteq U\) with exceptional set \(A\cup E\).  Fix the data in
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} on \(U\).  On each branch in
\(A\cup E\), choose a distance \(\sigma_i\) small enough that the
corresponding point lies in \(W\); take
\(\sigma_a\leq\rho_a\) for \(a\in A\) and, when \(e\in E\cap F\),
\(\sigma_e\leq r_e\).  The balance inequality on \(W\) with empty
full-branch set shows that every value sampled on the exceptional
branches \(A\cup E\) is finite: otherwise its right side would be
\(-\infty\).  Thus all the following rearrangements take place in
\(\mathbf R\).  By convexity, the secant slope
\eqref{eq:p071-star-secant-slope} increases when its distance decreases.
Therefore
\begin{align}
 \frac{u_a(-\sigma_a)-c}{\sigma_a}
   &\leq\frac{u_a(-\rho_a)-c}{\rho_a},
       &&a\in A,                                      \label{eq:p071-star-locality-a}\\
 \frac{u_e(-\sigma_e)-c}{\sigma_e}
   &\leq-\frac{c-u_e(-r_e)}{r_e},
       &&e\in E\cap F.                                \label{eq:p071-star-locality-e}
\end{align}
If \(e\in E\setminus F\), then \(e\) is a full branch of \(U\), so the
preceding branch argument gives \(u_e\leq c\), and its contribution on
the right side of the inequality on \(W\) is nonpositive.  Apply
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} on \(W\) to \(F\setminus E\),
use \eqref{eq:p071-star-locality-a}--\eqref{eq:p071-star-locality-e},
discard the nonpositive terms indexed by \(E\setminus F\), and move the
terms indexed by \(E\cap F\) to the left.  The result is exactly
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} on \(U\).

Branchwise convexity is local-to-global on an interval: on a compact
subinterval, take a finite interval cover on which convexity holds,
subdivide so that consecutive triples lie in members of the cover, and
use monotonicity of consecutive secant slopes.  The extended-real
open-stratum alternative from the first paragraph, together with the
possible polar endpoint jump, handles the value \(-\infty\).
The endpoint trace is local because any neighbourhood of \(-\infty\)
contains a complete terminal interval.  These observations, together
with the preceding restriction and gluing arguments, prove that
\(\mathscr J_B\) is a subsheaf.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Stability under decreasing limits.}
Let \(u_n\downarrow u\) on a standard neighbourhood.  Branchwise
extended-real convexity passes directly to the limit.  The exact trace
at a full endpoint also passes.  For completeness, put
\(c_n=u_n(-\infty)\) and \(c=u(-\infty)\).  Every function on a full
branch, including a polar one, is nondecreasing in the extended order,
so
\[
 c\leq \lim_{t\to-\infty}u(t).
\]
If \(c\in\mathbf R\), choose \(n\) with \(c_n<c+\varepsilon\), and then
take \(t\) sufficiently negative that
\(u(t)\leq u_n(t)<c+2\varepsilon\).  If \(c=-\infty\), the same argument
starts with \(c_n<M-1\) for an arbitrary \(M\in\mathbf R\).  This gives
the reverse trace inequality in both cases.

It remains to pass
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance}.  Suppose
\(u(\eta)=c\in\mathbf R\), and put \(c_n=u_n(\eta)\downarrow c\).
All full-branch terms on the left side for \(u_n\) are nonnegative.  No
sampled exceptional value can tend to \(-\infty\), since then the finite
right side would tend to \(-\infty\): every other exceptional value is
bounded above by its value for \(u_1\).  No sampled full-branch value can
tend to \(-\infty\), since then the left side would tend to \(+\infty\)
while the right side remains bounded above.  Thus every sampled limit is
finite, and termwise passage to the limit proves
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} for \(u\).  Hence
\(\mathscr J_B\) is stable under pointwise decreasing sequential limits.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Smooth psh functions satisfy the comparison conditions.}
Let \(f\) be smooth and psh on a standard neighbourhood, write
\(c=f(\eta)\), and set \(d_i=f_i'(0)\).  Branchwise positivity gives
convexity.  A full branch is constant near \(-\infty\), so \(d_b\geq0\)
for \(b\notin A\).  Smoothness gives
\[
             \sum_{b\notin A}d_b+\sum_{a\in A}d_a=0,
\]
with only finitely many nonzero terms.  By
\eqref{eq:p071-star-secant-below-derivative},
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{b\in F}\frac{c-f_b(-r_b)}{r_b}
 &\leq \sum_{b\notin A}d_b
  =-\sum_{a\in A}d_a\\
 &\leq \sum_{a\in A}\frac{f_a(-\rho_a)-c}{\rho_a}.
\end{align*}
The endpoint trace follows from the constant collar.  Thus every smooth
psh generator belongs to \(\mathscr J_B\).  The sheaf and limit properties
just proved, together with the minimal definition of
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}\), give
\begin{equation}
                   \operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}
                         \subseteq\mathscr J_B.
 \label{eq:p071-star-psh-in-comparison}
\end{equation}
This argument applies at every transfinite stage without intersecting a
countable family of neighbourhoods.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Finite centre: slopes and countable activity.}
Let \(u\in\mathscr J_B(U)\) and suppose that \(c=u(\eta)\) is finite.
Shrink the exceptional collars so that every closed interval
\([-R_a,0]\) used below remains in the original domain.  Taking \(F\)
empty in \eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-point-balance} shows that every
exceptional finite-stratum value is finite: one value \(-\infty\) would
make the right side \(-\infty\).  The same inequality with a singleton
full-branch set shows that every finite-stratum value on a full branch is
finite.  Hence all these branch functions are ordinarily continuous on
their open finite strata.

For an exceptional branch, \(d_a=D_-u_a(0)\) is bounded below by any
finite secant slope.  It cannot be \(+\infty\): keep the other
\(\rho_{a'}\) fixed and let \(\rho_a\downarrow0\) in the inequality with
\(F\) empty; the right side would tend to \(-\infty\).  Thus every
\(d_a\) is real.  A singleton full-branch inequality bounds
\(d_b\in[0,+\infty)\) from above.  Finiteness of these endpoint
derivatives rules out an upward jump at \(0\): for any fixed small
\(r_0>0\), convexity gives
\[
 \frac{c-u_i(-r_0)}{r_0}
   \leq \frac{c-u_i(-r)}r
   \leq d_i\qquad(0<r\leq r_0),
\]
so \(u_i(-r)\to c\).  Thus every branch function is continuous up to
\(0\).  Now let all \(r_b\downarrow0\) for a
fixed finite \(F\), and then let all \(\rho_a\downarrow0\).  We obtain
\begin{equation}
                   \sum_{b\in F}d_b
                       \leq-\sum_{a\in A}d_a.
 \label{eq:p071-star-finite-slope-bound}
\end{equation}
Taking the supremum over finite \(F\) proves
\eqref{eq:p071-star-slope-balance}.  A family of nonnegative real numbers
with bounded finite subsums has countable positive support: for each
\(m\geq1\), only finitely many can be at least \(1/m\).  Finally, a full
branch with \(d_b=0\) is constant, since
\[
             0\leq\frac{c-u_b(-r)}r\leq d_b=0
\]
for every finite \(r>0\), and the endpoint trace then gives
\(u_b(-\infty)=c\).  Thus the nonconstant full branches form a countable
set.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Finite harmonic smoothing.}
We prove the approximation statement used in the final construction.
Consider a fixed standard neighbourhood and a real-valued continuous
function \(h\) on its closure such that only finitely many branches are
nonconstant, each branch function is convex, each full branch has the
exact finite endpoint trace, all branch values at \(\eta\) equal \(c_h\),
all endpoint derivatives \(D_-h_i(0)\) are finite real numbers, and
\begin{equation}
                        \sum_iD_-h_i(0)\leq0.
 \label{eq:p071-star-smoothing-input-balance}
\end{equation}
Only finitely many terms are nonzero, so this is an ordinary finite
sum.  We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\), there is a
smooth psh function \(H\) on the same open neighbourhood with
\begin{equation}
                         \lVert H-h\rVert_\infty<\delta.
 \label{eq:p071-star-finite-smoothing-error}
\end{equation}

On an exceptional closed collar, take a sufficiently fine finite
partition ending at \(0\) and form the chordal interpolant of \(h_i\).
On a full branch, first choose \(T_i<0\) so negative that replacing
\(h_i\) on \([-\infty,T_i]\) by the constant \(h_i(T_i)\) changes it by
less than an arbitrarily prescribed error; this is possible by the exact
endpoint trace and monotonicity.  Then use a fine chordal interpolant on
\([T_i,0]\).  The resulting piecewise-affine functions \(p_i\) are
convex and may be chosen within \(\delta/4\) of \(h_i\), are exactly
constant near every included
\(-\infty\), and have last slopes
\begin{equation}
                         s_i\leq D_-h_i(0).
 \label{eq:p071-star-chord-slope}
\end{equation}

We spell out a simultaneous smoothing which preserves both terminal
pieces exactly.  For every \(N\geq2\), choose a nonnegative product
mollifier \(\rho_N\in C^\infty_c((-1,1)^N)\), even in each variable and
of integral one, and set
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal M_\tau(x_1,\ldots,x_N)
   =\int_{\mathbf R^N}
      \max_{1\leq j\leq N}(x_j+\tau y_j)\rho_N(y)\,\mathrm dy .
 \label{eq:p071-star-exact-regularized-maximum}
\end{equation}
This is the convolution of the maximum with a smooth compactly supported
kernel.  It is smooth, convex, nondecreasing in each variable, and
\[
 \left|\mathcal M_\tau(x)-\max_jx_j\right|\leq\tau.
\]
If, for some \(k\), \(x_k>x_j+2\tau\) for all \(j\ne k\), then the same
coordinate realizes the maximum throughout the support of \(\rho_N\).
Evenness gives \(\int y_k\rho_N(y)\,\mathrm dy=0\), and hence
\begin{equation}
                    \mathcal M_\tau(x)=x_k .
 \label{eq:p071-star-exact-dominance}
\end{equation}

Write a nonaffine \(p_i\) as the maximum of the affine extensions
\(\ell_{i1},\ldots,\ell_{iN_i}\) of its pieces.  Consecutive identical
pieces are first merged.  The last affine piece then strictly dominates
all the others at \(0\), and hence by a fixed positive margin on a
collar of \(0\).  On a full branch, its first, constant affine piece
strictly dominates all the others sufficiently far to the left.  Indeed,
after the merging, every other piece has positive slope there.  Choose
\(\tau>0\) smaller than half all these finitely many dominance margins
and also smaller than \(\delta/4\), and define
\[
 k_i(t)=\mathcal M_\tau
       \bigl(\ell_{i1}(t),\ldots,\ell_{iN_i}(t)\bigr).
\]
For an affine \(p_i\), simply take \(k_i=p_i\).  Convexity and coordinate
monotonicity of \(\mathcal M_\tau\) show that every \(k_i\) is smooth
and convex.  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-star-exact-regularized-maximum} and
\eqref{eq:p071-star-exact-dominance} show, respectively, that
\[

 \qquad k_i(0)=c_h,\qquad k_i'(0)=s_i,
\]
and that \(k_i\) is exactly constant on a collar of every included full
endpoint.  Put
\[
                         m=-\sum_i s_i\geq0,
\]
where nonnegativity follows from
\eqref{eq:p071-star-smoothing-input-balance} and
\eqref{eq:p071-star-chord-slope}.

Choose one branch.  On a sufficiently short collar \([-\ell,0]\), take
a smooth function \(\beta\) whose derivative increases from \(0\) to
\(m\), is identically \(0\) to the left of that collar, and is identically
\(m\) near \(0\), normalized by \(\beta(0)=0\).  Explicitly, for a smooth
nondecreasing cutoff \(\chi\) which is \(0\) near \(0\) and \(1\) near
\(1\), one may prescribe
\[
 \beta'(t)=m\chi\!\left(\frac{t+\ell}{\ell}\right)
      \quad(-\ell\leq t\leq0),
 \qquad
 \beta(t)=-\int_t^0\beta'(s)\,\mathrm ds,
\]
and extend \(\beta\) constantly to the left.  Then
\(\beta''\geq0\), \(\beta'(0)=m\), and
\(-m\ell\leq\beta\leq0\).  Add \(\beta\) to the smoothed function on
the chosen branch, leaving all other branches unchanged and every
inactive branch equal to \(c_h\).  By choosing \(\ell\) sufficiently
small, the additional error is less than \(\delta/2\).  The endpoint
derivatives now sum to zero exactly.  The explicit CLD description in
\eqref{eq:p071-star-smooth-balance} shows that the glued function \(H\)
is smooth, including at \(\eta\); branchwise convexity gives
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''H\geq0\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:p071-star-finite-smoothing-error}.  Notice that the amplitude
of the derivative repair tends to zero with \(\ell\), even when \(m\)
is large.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{A decreasing approximation on one fixed neighbourhood.}
Return to a finite-centre \(u\in\mathscr J_B(U)\), after the preceding
shrinking.  Enumerate the nonconstant full branches as
\(C=\{b_1,b_2,\ldots\}\), stopping if \(C\) is finite.  For \(n\geq1\),
define \(w_n\) by
\begin{align}
 w_{n,a}&=\max\{u_a,c-n\}, &&a\in A,                 \label{eq:p071-star-truncation-a}\\
 w_{n,b_j}&=\max\{u_{b_j},c-n\}, &&j\leq n,          \label{eq:p071-star-truncation-b}\\
 w_{n,b}&=c, &&b\notin A\cup\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}.     \label{eq:p071-star-truncation-inactive}
\end{align}
The maximum of a convex function and a constant is convex.  The exact
trace on a full branch shows that the truncated function is finite and
continuous at \(-\infty\); on an exceptional branch it is finite and
continuous on the chosen closed collar.  Thus \(w_n\) is a finite
continuous branchwise-convex function on the closed standard star, with
only finitely many active branches.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
                        w_{n+1}\leq w_n,
                        \qquad w_n\longrightarrow u
                        \quad\text{pointwise}.
 \label{eq:p071-star-truncations-decrease}
\end{equation}
Since truncation is inactive on a sufficiently short collar of \(0\),
the endpoint derivatives of \(w_n\) are \(d_a\), \(a\in A\), and
\(d_{b_j}\), \(j\leq n\).  Therefore
\[
             \sum_{a\in A}d_a+\sum_{j\leq n}d_{b_j}\leq0
\]
by \eqref{eq:p071-star-slope-balance}.  Apply the finite harmonic
smoothing just proved to \(w_n+\varepsilon_n\), where
\[
                \varepsilon_n=2^{-n},
                \qquad \delta_n=2^{-(n+4)}.
\]
It gives a smooth psh \(g_n\) on the same fixed open neighbourhood with
\begin{equation}
                  \lVert g_n-(w_n+\varepsilon_n)\rVert_\infty
                         <\delta_n.
 \label{eq:p071-star-smoothing-diagonal-error}
\end{equation}
For every point of that neighbourhood,
\begin{align*}
 g_n-g_{n+1}
 &> (w_n-w_{n+1})+(\varepsilon_n-\varepsilon_{n+1})
            -\delta_n-\delta_{n+1}\\
 &\geq 2^{-(n+1)}-2^{-(n+4)}-2^{-(n+5)}>0.
\end{align*}
Thus \(g_n\) decreases on one fixed neighbourhood.  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-star-truncations-decrease} and
\eqref{eq:p071-star-smoothing-diagonal-error} show pointwise convergence
to \(u\), including at every \(-\infty\)-endpoint.  This proves
\(\mathscr J_B\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}\) at a finite-centre
germ.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Centre value \(-\infty\) and the remaining points.}
Suppose \(u\in\mathscr J_B\) and \(u(\eta)=-\infty\).  On a full branch,
the exact trace and convexity make the branch function nondecreasing, so
every value is at most \(u(0)=-\infty\); hence the whole full branch is
identically \(-\infty\).  On an exceptional collar, convexity with the
endpoint value \(-\infty\) forces the function to be \(-\infty\) on a
smaller collar.  Since there are only finitely many exceptional branches,
one simultaneous shrinking makes \(u\equiv-\infty\).  The smooth psh
constants \(-n\) decrease to this germ.

At an interior point of a branch, local extended-real convexity gives
either the identically \(-\infty\) case or an ordinary finite convex
function.  On a smaller relatively compact interval, extend it to a
finite convex function on \(\mathbf R\) by affine supporting rays.  If
\(P_s\) denotes convolution with the centred Gaussian of variance
\(2s\), then \(P_su\) is smooth and convex.  The semigroup identity and
Jensen's inequality give
\[
               0<s'<s\quad\Longrightarrow\quad P_{s'}u\leq P_su,
\]
and \(P_su\to u\) locally uniformly as \(s\downarrow0\).  The sequence
\(P_{1/n}u\) therefore gives the required fixed-interval approximation.

For clarity, we also give the endpoint construction.  Let \(v\) be a
branch function on \([-\infty,R)\) satisfying
\eqref{eq:p071-star-endpoint-trace}.  The identically \(-\infty\) case
is handled by constants.  Otherwise \(v\) is finite, convex, and
nondecreasing on the finite stratum.  Choose
\[
                         r<R_1<R_2<R
\]
and extend \(v|_{(-\infty,R_1]}\) to a finite convex nondecreasing
function \(\bar v\) on \(\mathbf R\) by the affine ray of slope
\[
                  \frac{v(R_2)-v(R_1)}{R_2-R_1}
\]
to the right of \(R_1\).  All slopes of \(\bar v\) lie in a bounded
interval, so its Gaussian regularizations
\(A_s=P_s\bar v\) are finite, smooth, convex, and nondecreasing, satisfy
\(A_{s'}\leq A_s\) for \(s'<s\), and converge uniformly to \(\bar v\)
with an error bounded by a constant times \(\sqrt{s}\).

Fix the two-variable regularized maximum
\(\mathcal M_\tau\) from
\eqref{eq:p071-star-exact-regularized-maximum} and put
\[
                         H_n(t)=\mathcal M_\tau(t,-n).
\]
Then \(H_n\) is smooth, convex, and nondecreasing, equals \(-n\) for
all sufficiently negative \(t\), equals \(t\) for every fixed finite
\(t\) and all sufficiently large \(n\), and
\(H_{n+1}\leq H_n\).  On the fixed endpoint neighbourhood
\([-\infty,r)\), define
\[
 F_n(t)=A_{1/n}(H_n(t)),\qquad
 F_n(-\infty)=A_{1/n}(-n).
\]
Every \(F_n\) is smooth and convex and is exactly constant on a
neighbourhood of \(-\infty\).  Moreover,
\[
 F_{n+1}=A_{1/(n+1)}\circ H_{n+1}
      \leq A_{1/n}\circ H_{n+1}
      \leq A_{1/n}\circ H_n=F_n.
\]
At a finite point, eventual equality \(H_n(t)=t\) and the heat error
give \(F_n(t)\to v(t)\).  At \(-\infty\), the same error gives
\[
             F_n(-\infty)-v(-n)\longrightarrow0,
\]
while the exact trace gives
\(v(-n)\to v(-\infty)\) in
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\).  Thus \(F_n\downarrow v\) pointwise on
one fixed endpoint neighbourhood, including when
\(v(-\infty)=-\infty\).

We have proved
\(\mathscr J_B\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}\) at every point.
Together with \eqref{eq:p071-star-psh-in-comparison} and the tautological
inclusions
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B,1}\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X_B}\), this is
\eqref{eq:p071-star-first-stage-collapse} and all the additional
assertions of the theorem.
\end{proof}

We divide the proof into source-legality, a countable-factor comparison
sheaf, and a fixed-neighbourhood regularization.

First consider \(Z\) alone.  Its topology satisfies
\cite[\S3.1.1]{CLD25}: local compactness and the clopen-basis hypothesis
give a basis of relatively compact open subsets, hence a basis of open
subsets that are countable at infinity.  Locally closed subsets satisfy the
domain axioms of \cite[\S3.1.2]{CLD25}.  Indeed, the first three axioms are
immediate from the definition, and every locally closed subset is itself a
locally compact space with a clopen basis; its compact clopen
neighbourhoods form the required \(G\)-cover by compact domains.

The locally constant real-valued functions form a \(G\)-sheaf.  To check
the only nonformal point, suppose compatible locally constant functions are
glued across a \(G\)-cover.  At a given point, use the finite subfamily in
the definition of a \(G\)-cover.  Intersect ordinary neighbourhoods on
which the finitely many restrictions are constant.  Their union contains
a neighbourhood of the point in the domain, and compatibility makes the
glued function constant there.

A locally constant map from a compact domain has finite image.  In the
standing \((\mathbf Q,\mathbf R)\)-convention of
\cite[\S1.8.2]{CLD25}, every finite subset of \(\mathbf R^m\) is a compact
polyhedron.  Parlinear composition preserves local constancy.  The inverse
image of any subset under a locally constant map is clopen in its domain,
so in particular the inverse image of a parlinear subspace is a domain.
This verifies all the axioms in \cite[\S3.1.3]{CLD25}.

Take the affine presheaf \(L_Z\) equal to this parlinear sheaf.  It contains
the constants, ordinary local gluing preserves local constancy, and a
function is parlinear if and only if it is \(G\)-locally affine.  Thus the
two affinage axioms of \cite[\S6.1.1]{CLD25} hold.  Consequently the data
in the statement make \(Z\) an affine \(G\)-tropical space of tropical
dimension zero.

The product with the standard affine space \(\Omega\) is legitimate by
\cite[\S\S9.1.1--9.1.4]{CLD25}.  Product affine functions are locally sums
of locally constant functions of \(z\) and affine functions of \(x\).
It follows from \cite[Definition~6.2.1]{CLD25} that, after a clopen
shrinking in the \(Z\)-factor, a smooth function is a smooth function of
the Euclidean variable alone, and conversely.  The formula for
\(\mathrm d'\mathrm d''\) and positivity are therefore the ordinary
Hessian formula and positive-semidefiniteness on the Euclidean factor.
This proves source-legality and the asserted description of the smooth psh
generators.

Define \(\mathscr Q\) to be the sheaf of functions with values in
\(\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) which locally have the following form.  There
are a compact clopen \(C\subseteq Z\), an open ball
\(B\Subset\Omega\), a compact metrizable space \(Y\) with a clopen basis, a
continuous surjection \(q:C\to Y\), and an upper semicontinuous function
\(\bar v:Y\times B\to\mathbf R\cup\{-\infty\}\) such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-local-factor}
                  v(z,x)=\bar v(q(z),x),
\end{equation}
and, for every \(y\in Y\), \(x\mapsto\bar v(y,x)\) is either finite-valued
convex or identically \(-\infty\).  This is a sheaf because the condition
is local.  Every smooth psh function belongs to
\(\mathscr Q\): shrink until it is independent of \(z\), take \(Y\) to be
a point, and use positivity of its Euclidean Hessian.

We next prove that \(\mathscr Q\) is stable under decreasing sequential

every \(v_n\in\mathscr Q(W)\), and fix a point.  Choose a compact clopen
\(C\subseteq Z\) and a ball \(B_0\Subset\Omega\) such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-compact-core}
                         C\times\overline{B_0}\subseteq W.
\end{equation}
For each
fixed \(n\), compactness gives a finite cover of
\(C\times\overline{B_0}\) by product sets
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-factor-cover}
                       C_{n,a}\times B_{n,a},
\end{equation}
where \(C_{n,a}\) is compact clopen in \(C\), \(B_{n,a}\) is open, and on this
product \(v_n\) factors through a compact metrizable zero-dimensional
quotient \(q_{n,a}:C_{n,a}\to Y_{n,a}\).

Choose a countable clopen base \(\mathcal D_{n,a}\) of every \(Y_{n,a}\).
Let \(\mathcal B\) be the Boolean subalgebra of the clopen subsets of \(C\)
generated by all the sets \(C_{n,a}\) and all the sets
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-boolean-generators}
                  q_{n,a}^{-1}(D),
                  \qquad D\in\mathcal D_{n,a}.
\end{equation}
viewed as clopen subsets of \(C\).  There are countably many generators.
Declare two points of \(C\) equivalent when they belong to the same members
of \(\mathcal B\), and let
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-common-quotient}
                  q:C\longrightarrow
                  Y:=q(C)\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal B}.
\end{equation}
Every coordinate of \(q\) is the characteristic function of a clopen set,
so \(q\) is continuous and is surjective by the definition of \(Y\).
The space \(Y\) is compact, metrizable, and zero-dimensional.

Every \(v_n|_{C\times B_0}\) is constant on the fibres of
\(q\times\operatorname{id}_{B_0}\).  Indeed, if \(q(z)=q(z')\) and
\(x\in B_0\), choose a member of the finite cover
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-factor-cover} containing
\((z,x)\).  Membership in \(C_{n,a}\) is recorded in \(\mathcal B\), so
\(z'\in C_{n,a}\).  Membership in the inverse images of the countable

\(q_{n,a}(z)=q_{n,a}(z')\), and the local factorization gives

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-limit-factor}
                         v(z,x)=\bar v(q(z),x).
\end{equation}

The function \(\bar v\) is upper semicontinuous.  Here is the quotient

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-sublevel-union}

\end{equation}

\(N\times D\subseteq\{v<t\}\).  The map \(q\) is closed because its source

\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-quotient-neighbourhood}
                       Y\setminus q(C\setminus N)

A locally extended-real convex function

 \leq a_{k+1}(q(z),x)+\eta_{k+1}
 \leq a_k(q(z),x)+\eta_{k+1}
 \leq w_k(z,x)+\eta_{k+1}.
\end{equation}
Set
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-tail-correction}
                       c_k=\sum_{j\geq k+1}\eta_j,
             \qquad   g_k=w_k+c_k.
\end{equation}
Then \(c_k=\eta_{k+1}+c_{k+1}\), so
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-almost-monotone} implies \(g_{k+1}\leq g_k\).
Finally, \eqref{eq:p071-stone-envelope-convergence},
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-mollification-error}, and \(c_k\to0\) show
that \(g_k\downarrow v\) on \(C\times B\).  This proves the reverse
inclusion when \(d>0\).

If \(d=0\), the unique nonempty open subset of \(\mathbf R^0\) is a point.
Give \(Y\) a compatible metric and choose nested finite clopen partitions
\(\mathcal P_k\) whose mesh tends to zero, exactly as above.  Put
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:p071-stone-zero-dimensional-envelope}
        a_{k,P}=\max\{-k,\sup_{y\in P}\bar v(y)\},
        \qquad w_k(z)=a_{k,P_k(q(z))}.
\end{equation}
The functions \(w_k\) are locally constant, hence smooth psh.  Refinement
and the lower truncations show that they decrease.  Upper semicontinuity
and the shrinking mesh give \(w_k\downarrow v\), by the same argument as
for \eqref{eq:p071-stone-envelope-convergence}.  Thus the conclusion holds
without Euclidean mollification or a tail correction.

We have proved
\(\mathscr Q\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\) in every dimension.
Together with \eqref{eq:p071-stone-minimality} and the tautological
inclusion
\(\operatorname{Psh}_{X,1}\subseteq\operatorname{Psh}_X\), this proves
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-collapse}--\eqref{eq:p071-stone-factorization}, as
well as the fixed-neighbourhood assertion
\eqref{eq:p071-stone-fixed-neighbourhood}.

For the displayed example, the Cantor cube \(\{0,1\}^{\Lambda}\) is compact,
Hausdorff, and zero-dimensional for every \(\Lambda\).  When \(\Lambda\) is
uncountable it is generally nonmetrizable, but every function produced by
the hierarchy locally factors through the metrizable quotient constructed
in \eqref{eq:p071-stone-common-quotient}; no metrizability of \(Z\) was
used.  This also makes clear why
the argument does not extend to a nontrivial affine structure in the
\(Z\)-direction or to general polyhedral face gluings.

\begin{proof}
Write $c(y)=u(\eta,y)$ near the node.  We use the comparison theorem
\Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate}, including its endpoint
trace, slope budget, finite-activity truncation, and finite harmonic
smoothing.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Locality and decreasing closure of the comparison conditions.}
The definition of $\mathcal J_X$ is local, so restriction and gluing are
immediate once the product junction inequality is known to be local.  To
check this point, contract every point occurring in
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-jensen} by a common factor
$0<s<1$ towards $(\eta,y_0)$:
\[
 (-r_i,y_i)\longmapsto
 (-sr_i,\,y_0+s(y_i-y_0)).
\]
The barycentre relation is preserved, with every reciprocal weight
multiplied by $s^{-1}$.  For sufficiently small $s$, all contracted
points lie in one comparison chart at $(\eta,y_0)$.  Write the exceptional
set of that restricted chart as $A\cup E$, enlarging $E\subset B\setminus
A$ harmlessly if necessary.  Retain the contracted data on every original
tuple branch in $A\cup F$.  For each newly exceptional branch
$e\in E\setminus F$, choose any $0<\sigma_e$ in its restricted collar
and add the sample $(-\sigma_e,y_0)$.  The enlarged barycentre relation
still holds, because the new point and the centre have the same Euclidean
coordinate.  With
\[
                  \Theta=\sum_{e\in E\setminus F}\frac1{\sigma_e},
\]
the restricted-chart inequality is
\begin{align*}
 (s^{-1}\Lambda+\Theta)c(y_0)
 &\leq \sum_{b\in F}
   \frac{u_b(-sr_b,y_0+s(y_b-y_0))}{sr_b}\\
 &\quad+\sum_{a\in A}
   \frac{u_a(-s\rho_a,y_0+s(y_a-y_0))}{s\rho_a}
   +\sum_{e\in E\setminus F}
   \frac{u_e(-\sigma_e,y_0)}{\sigma_e}.
\end{align*}
Each newly exceptional branch was full before restriction, so its last
sample is at most $c(y_0)$.  Joint convexity on each original segment gives
\[
 u_i(-sr_i,y_0+s(y_i-y_0))
 \leq (1-s)c(y_0)+s u_i(-r_i,y_i).
\]
Substitution bounds the right side of the restricted-chart inequality by
\[
 (s^{-1}-1)\Lambda c(y_0)
 +\sum_{b\in F}\frac{u_b(-r_b,y_b)}{r_b}
 +\sum_{a\in A}\frac{u_a(-\rho_a,y_a)}{\rho_a}
 +\Theta c(y_0).
\]
Cancelling the two added central contributions proves the original
inequality.  The same argument proves compatibility when a full branch
becomes exceptional after restriction.  Thus the displayed conditions do
define a sheaf.

We next prove sequential closure.  Let $u_n\downarrow u$ on an open set
and fix a node point.  Choose a standard product
$U_0\times V_0$ in that open set and a compact convex set
$Q\Subset V_0$ whose interior contains the Euclidean coordinate of the
point.  For fixed $n$, compactness of $\{\eta\}\times Q$ supplies
finitely many comparison charts for $u_n$.  The union of their finite
exceptional sets and countable activity sets is countable; call it
$K_n$.  Local joint convexity and the contraction argument above extend
the branch and junction conditions across $U_0\times\operatorname{int}Q$.
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 u_n(p_b(t),y)=u_n(\eta,y)
 \quad
 \bigl(b\notin A\cup K_n,\ t\in[-\infty,0],\ y\in Q\bigr),
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-limit-inactive}
\end{equation}
where $A$ is the finite exceptional set of $U_0$.  Hence the limit has
one countable activity set $\bigcup_nK_n$.

Joint extended-real convexity passes to a decreasing limit.  For each fixed
$y$, the endpoint trace passes by the argument in the exact-star theorem:
monotonicity gives one inequality, and a sufficiently advanced row gives
the reverse inequality, also when the limiting endpoint value is
$-\infty$.  The same specialization, with every Euclidean sample equal
to $y$, shows that each fibre is a member of $\mathscr J_B$.
Suppose now that $c(y_0)$ is finite in a prescribed product junction
tuple.  The scalar exact-star argument shows that every finite-stratum
value in that tuple is finite.  Consequently all terms in the junction
inequality for $u_n$ converge in $\mathbf R$, and termwise passage to
the limit proves \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-jensen} for $u$.
Thus $\mathcal J_X$ is closed under pointwise decreasing sequential
limits.

Every generator belongs to $\mathcal J_X$.  Only the product junction
condition requires proof.  Put
$d_i=\partial_tg_i(0,y_0)$.  Joint convexity and smoothness give
\[
 g_i(-r_i,y_i)\geq
 c_g(y_0)-r_id_i+
 \nabla c_g(y_0)\mathbin\cdot(y_i-y_0),
\]
where $r_i$ denotes $r_b$ or $\rho_a$.  Divide by $r_i$ and sum
over the selected full branches and all exceptional branches.  The
Euclidean linear terms cancel by
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-barycentre}.  Every omitted full-branch
derivative is nonnegative, since that branch is convex and constant near
$-\infty$.  The balance law
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-smooth-balance} therefore says that the
sum of the selected derivatives is nonpositive.  The remaining inequality
is exactly \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-jensen}.  Minimality now gives
\begin{equation}
                         \mathcal P_X\subseteq\mathcal J_X.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-minimality}
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Partial Legendre reduction at a finite node value.}
Let $u\in\mathcal J_X$ near $(\eta,y_0)$, and first suppose that
$c(y_0)\in\mathbf R$.  After shrinking the Euclidean ball, $c$ is
finite: an extended-real convex function on an open convex set cannot take
both a finite value and the value $-\infty$.  Specializing the product
junction condition to equal Euclidean coordinates places every fibre in
$\mathscr J_B$.  The finite-centre part of the exact-star theorem then
shows that all finite-stratum branch values are real.

Use a comparison chart on $U\times V_0$, with exceptional set $A$ and
countable activity set $K$.  Shrink the exceptional collars once.  Let
$D\subset U$ be the resulting compact closed standard core.  Choose an
open convex set $V\ni y_0$ and a compact convex set $Q$ such that
\[
                  \overline V\subset\operatorname{int}Q,
                  \qquad Q\Subset V_0.
\]
For
$p\in(\mathbf R^d)^*$, define
\begin{align}
 f_0(p)&=\min_{y\in Q}\bigl(c(y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr),
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-legendre-centre}\\
 f_b(t,p)&=\min_{y\in Q}
       \bigl(u_b(t,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-legendre-branch}
\end{align}
At a full endpoint the second minimum is interpreted in the extended
order.  Its endpoint slice is either finite on the interior of $Q$ or
identically $-\infty$; these are the only possibilities for an
extended-real convex function on a connected open convex set.

For every fixed $p$, the functions in
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-legendre-centre}--%
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-legendre-branch} form a member
$f(\,cdot\,,p)\in\mathscr J_B(D)$.  Convexity in the branch variable
follows by taking minimizing Euclidean points at two branch parameters and
using their convex combination in $Q$.  For a full branch, exact endpoint
trace passes through the minimum: the lower bound follows from
monotonicity, while evaluation at a minimizing endpoint point gives the
upper bound; if the endpoint slice is $-\infty$, evaluation at any fixed
Euclidean point gives convergence to $-\infty$.

It remains to check the finite-point balance.  Choose minimizing points
$y_i\in Q$ for all finitely many branch terms and set
\[
 y_*=\Lambda^{-1}
 \left(\sum_{b\in F}\frac{y_b}{r_b}
       +\sum_{a\in A}\frac{y_a}{\rho_a}\right)\in Q.
\]
Then the product junction inequality gives
\begin{align*}
 \Lambda f_0(p)
 &\leq \Lambda\bigl(c(y_*)-p\mathbin\cdot y_*\bigr)\\
 &\leq
 \sum_{b\in F}\frac{f_b(-r_b,p)}{r_b}
 +\sum_{a\in A}\frac{f_a(-\rho_a,p)}{\rho_a}.
\end{align*}
This is the Jensen form of the scalar exact-star balance.  Finally,
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-countable-activity} gives
\begin{equation}
 f_b(t,p)=f_0(p)
 \quad(b\in B\setminus(A\cup K)).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-legendre-inactive}
\end{equation}

Conversely, suppose that scalar profiles $h_b(t,p)$ belong to
$\mathscr J_B(D)$ for every $p$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 H_b(t,y)=\sup_p\bigl(p\mathbin\cdot y+h_b(t,p)\bigr)
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-reconstruction}
\end{equation}
is jointly convex on every branch and satisfies the product junction
condition.  Indeed, multiply the scalar Jensen inequality by the
reciprocal-distance weights, add the Euclidean barycentre identity, and
then take the supremum in $p$.  This observation is the bridge between
the scalar exact-star smoothing and the mixed Hessian required here.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{Finite activity and finite dual sampling.}
Choose nested finite sets $K_n\subset K$ with union $K$, stopping if
$K$ is finite.  Define scalar profiles, for every $p$, by
\begin{align}
 h_{n,a}(t,p)&=\max\{f_a(t,p),f_0(p)-n\}, &&a\in A,
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-truncate-a}\\
 h_{n,b}(t,p)&=\max\{f_b(t,p),f_0(p)-n\}, &&b\in K_n,
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-truncate-k}\\
 h_{n,b}(t,p)&=f_0(p), &&b\in B\setminus(A\cup K_n).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-truncate-rest}
\end{align}
The slope-budget and truncation argument in the exact-star theorem shows
that each $h_n(\,cdot\,,p)$ is a finite continuous, finite-active member
of $\mathscr J_B(D)$.  It also gives
\begin{equation}
 h_{n+1}(x,p)\leq h_n(x,p),
 \qquad h_n(x,p)\longrightarrow f_x(p).
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-profile-limit}
\end{equation}
On a newly retained branch, the first inequality uses
$f_b(t,p)\leq f_0(p)$, the monotonicity of a full scalar comparison
profile towards the node.

Let $H_n$ be reconstructed from $h_n$ by
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-reconstruction}.  Local convex
biconjugacy on $\operatorname{int}Q$ gives the explicit formula
\begin{equation}
 H_{n,b}(t,y)=
 \begin{cases}
  \max\{u_b(t,y),c(y)-n\},&b\in A\cup K_n,\\
  c(y),&b\in B\setminus(A\cup K_n).
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-truncated-reconstruction}
\end{equation}
The formula remains valid at a full endpoint: if the endpoint slice is
finite, use its supporting covectors; if it is identically $-\infty$,
only the second entry of the maximum remains.  Hence
\begin{equation}
 H_{n+1}\leq H_n,
 \qquad H_n\longrightarrow u
 \quad\text{pointwise on }D\times V.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-H-limit}
\end{equation}

Each $H_n$ is finite and continuous on
$D\times\overline V$.  On finite branch strata this follows from finite
joint convexity.  We record why pointwise continuity in the branch
variable is enough at the node.  If a finite convex function $q$ on
$[-R,0]\times V_0$ has continuous boundary value
$q(0,y)=c_q(y)$ and
$q(t,y)\to c_q(y)$ for every fixed $y$, then $q$ is continuous at
every point of $\{0\}\times V_0$.  For the upper bound, write a nearby
$(t,y)$ as a convex combination of $(0,z)$ and $(-R,w)$, with
$w$ fixed and the coefficient of $(-R,w)$ tending to zero.  For the
lower bound, first choose $t_0<0$ so that
$q(t_0,y_0)$ is close to $c_q(y_0)$, then write
$(t_0,y_0)$ as a convex combination of the nearby $(t,y)$ and a point
$(-R,z)$.  Solving the convexity inequality for $q(t,y)$, and using
boundedness of the finite convex slice $q(-R,\,\cdot\,)$ on a compact
Euclidean neighbourhood, gives the lower bound.  This proves the claim.

Only finitely many branches of $H_n$ are active.  Apply the boundary lemma
to each of them.  The scalar endpoint-slope bounds give its fixed-$y$
hypothesis, while every inactive branch is exactly $c(y)$.  The
cofinite-branch topology now gives continuity at the node.

At a full endpoint, choose any sequence of branch parameters decreasing to
$-\infty$.  Equations
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-endpoint-trace} and
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-truncated-reconstruction} give monotone
convergence of the corresponding continuous Euclidean slices to the finite
convex endpoint slice.  Dini's theorem makes this convergence uniform on
$\overline V$; branch monotonicity then makes the estimate uniform for all
sufficiently terminal parameters.  Since $D$ is compact, so is
$D\times\overline V$.

Fix a summable positive sequence $(\varepsilon_n)$.  For each point of
that compact product, choose a covector which realizes
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-reconstruction} within
$\varepsilon_n$.  Continuity of the corresponding scalar profile on
$D$ supplies a neighbourhood on which the same choice works.  A finite
subcover gives covectors $p_{n,1},\ldots,p_{n,q_n}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 H_n-\varepsilon_n\leq
 A_n:=\max_j\bigl(p_{n,j}\mathbin\cdot y
                 +h_n(x,p_{n,j})\bigr)
 \leq H_n
 \quad\text{on }D\times\overline V.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-finite-dual-sampling}
\end{equation}
No compactness of the full dual space is used.

For each selected profile, truncation is inactive on a sufficiently short
node collar.  Its endpoint derivatives are therefore the finite derivatives
of the corresponding scalar comparison profile, and their sum is
nonpositive by the scalar slope balance.  Choose once a smaller standard
neighbourhood $U'$ with closure in $D$.  The finite harmonic smoothing
from the exact-star theorem then gives, for every selected covector, a smooth
psh scalar function $s_{n,j}$ on that same $U'$ with
\[
 \bigl\lVert s_{n,j}-h_n(\,cdot\,,p_{n,j})\bigr\rVert_{U'}
 <\varepsilon_n.
\]
Thus $s_{n,j}+2\varepsilon_n$ lies between the scalar profile plus
$\varepsilon_n$ and that profile plus $3\varepsilon_n$.  The lifted
function
\[
 (x,y)\longmapsto
 s_{n,j}(x)+2\varepsilon_n+p_{n,j}\mathbin\cdot y
\]
is an exact product generator.  Apply a smooth convex coordinatewise
nondecreasing regularized maximum to these finitely many lifts, with error
at most $\varepsilon_n$, and add one further $\varepsilon_n$.  The
result is a generator $W_n$ on $U'\times V$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
                         H_n\leq W_n\leq H_n+5\varepsilon_n.
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-smoothing-error}
\end{equation}
The balance law survives the regularized maximum.  At the node, its partial
derivatives with respect to the finitely many inputs are independent of the
branch, so summing first over the branches reduces
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-smooth-balance} to the corresponding
balance for each input.  A finite union of activity sets is finite, and a
common terminal collar exists for every full active branch.  Joint
convexity follows from convex monotone composition.

Set
\[
 d_n=5\sum_{k>n}\varepsilon_k,
 \qquad G_n=W_n+d_n.
\]
Equations \eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-H-limit} and
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-smoothing-error} give
\[
 G_{n+1}\leq H_{n+1}+5\varepsilon_{n+1}+d_{n+1}
 \leq H_n+d_n\leq G_n.
\]
Moreover, $G_n\to u$ pointwise.  This proves the fixed-neighbourhood
first-stage approximation at every finite node value.

\medskip\noindent
\emph{The value $-\infty$, full endpoints, and interior points.}
If $c(y_0)=-\infty$, joint convexity makes $c$ identically
$-\infty$ after a Euclidean shrinking.  On every full branch, the scalar
exact trace and convexity then force the whole branch to be
$-\infty$; on the finitely many exceptional collars, joint convexity
forces $-\infty$ after one common shrinking.  Thus the germ is
identically $-\infty$, and the constants $-n$ give the required
approximation.

It remains to treat a point $(-\infty,y_0)$ in a full branch.  Work on
$[ -\infty,R)\times V_0$, where $R<0$.  The identically $-\infty$
case is again immediate.  Otherwise the function is finite on the finite
stratum and is nondecreasing in the branch variable.  Choose $r<R_1<R$,
an open convex set $V\ni y_0$, and a compact convex set $Q$ with
$\overline V\subset\operatorname{int}Q\Subset V_0$, and put
\begin{align*}
 f(t,p)&=\min_{y\in Q}\bigl(u(t,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr),\\
 f_1(p)&=\min_{y\in Q}\bigl(u(R_1,y)-p\mathbin\cdot y\bigr),\\
 h_n(t,p)&=\max\{f(t,p),f_1(p)-n\}.
\end{align*}
Then $h_n(\,cdot\,,p)$ is finite, convex, nondecreasing, and has the
exact endpoint trace.  Its reconstruction is
\begin{equation}
 H_n(t,y)=\max\{u(t,y),u(R_1,y)-n\},
 \label{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-endpoint-truncation}
\end{equation}
so $H_n\downarrow u$ and every $H_n$ is continuous on the compact
terminal core $[ -\infty,r]\times\overline V$.  The endpoint continuity
again follows from Dini's theorem.

Fix a summable positive sequence $(\varepsilon_n)$.  Finite dual sampling
on the compact terminal core gives covectors
$p_{n,1},\ldots,p_{n,q_n}$ such that
\[
 H_n-\varepsilon_n\leq
 A_n:=\max_j\bigl(p_{n,j}\mathbin\cdot y
                 +h_n(t,p_{n,j})\bigr)\leq H_n.
\]
For each selected scalar profile, use the endpoint construction in the
proof of \Cref{thm:p071-infinite-star-collapse-candidate}.  It supplies a
decreasing sequence of smooth convex functions, constant on terminal
collars, with limit $h_n$.  Since $h_n$ is finite and continuous on the
compact endpoint interval, Dini's theorem permits the choice of one term
$s_{n,j}$ satisfying
\[
       h_n(\,cdot\,,p_{n,j})\leq s_{n,j}\leq
       h_n(\,cdot\,,p_{n,j})+\varepsilon_n.
\]
Add $2\varepsilon_n$ to the finitely many lifted functions
$s_{n,j}(t)+p_{n,j}\mathbin\cdot y$, apply the same regularized maximum
with error at most $\varepsilon_n$, and add one further
$\varepsilon_n$.  The resulting exact product generator $W_n$ satisfies
\[
                       H_n\leq W_n\leq H_n+5\varepsilon_n
\]
on one fixed terminal product neighbourhood.  The neighbourhood is
independent of $n$; only finitely many selected profiles occur at each
stage, so their constant collars have a common terminal subcollar.  Set
\[
 d_n=5\sum_{k>n}\varepsilon_k,\qquad G_n=W_n+d_n.
\]
Since $H_{n+1}\leq H_n$, the same calculation as at the node gives
\[
 G_{n+1}\leq H_{n+1}+5\varepsilon_{n+1}+d_{n+1}
 \leq H_n+d_n\leq G_n.
\]
Moreover $G_n\to u$ pointwise.  Thus the $G_n$ give the required
decreasing exact product generators on one fixed terminal neighbourhood.

At an interior branch point, a locally extended-real jointly convex
function is either identically $-\infty$ or finite.  In the finite case,
the point lies in an ordinary open convex chart in
$\mathbf R^{d+1}$.  The one-point Stone case of
\Cref{thm:p071-stone-euclidean-collapse} therefore gives a decreasing
smooth jointly convex approximation on one fixed smaller chart.  We have
therefore proved
$\mathcal J_X\subseteq\mathcal P_{X,1}$ at every point.  Together with
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-minimality} and the tautological inclusion
$\mathcal P_{X,1}\subseteq\mathcal P_X$, this proves
\eqref{eq:p071-infinite-euclidean-collapse} and the fixed-neighbourhood
assertions.
\end{proof}
